stem: The most abundant element found in the human body is –
expl: Nearly 99% of the mass of human body consists of just six chemical elements– oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, calcium and phosphorus. Oxygen is the most abundant element in the human body. It is mainly found in the form of water. Water, makes up generally about 55-70% of the human body and participates in countless metabolic reactions.

expl: Calcium phosphate is the principal form of calcium found in bovine milk and blood. About 70% of bone consists of hydroxyapatite, a calcium phosphate mineral (known as bone mineral). Up to 50% by volume and about 70% by weight of human bones is a modified form of hydroxyapatite.

stem: The number of bones in an adult human body is –
expl: The number of bones in an adult human body is 206. The body of a child has about 300 bones at birth, which decreases to 206 bones by adulthood after some bones have fused together. Together these bones form the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton.

stem: Which of the following is the smallest bone in the human body ?
expl: The stapes is the lightest stirrup-shaped bone and the smallest bone in the human body found in the middle of humans ears. While femur is the largest bone in the human body. It is located in the upper leg which connects the knee at one end and fits into the hip socket at the other.

stem: The number of bones in human skull is –
expl: The human skull (excluding hyoid bone of the neck) consists of 28 bones. It consists of two parts, neurocranium and the facial skeleton (also called the viscerocranium). Neurocranium has 8 bones and there are 14 in the viscerocranium (facial bones) and remaining 6 bones occurs in the middle ear, which is helpful in listening.

stem: The number of cervical vertebrae in a human body is:
expl: The human cervical spine comprises 7 vertebrae (C1 to C7) and is divided into 2 major segments. The 2 most cephalad vertebrae, the atlas (C1) and the axis (C2), form the craniocervical junction (CCJ) together with the occiput. The 5 cervical vertebrae caudad, C3 to C7, comprise the subaxial spine and are referred to by number. The cervical spine supports the weight of the cranium and head and neck motion.

stem: The type of joint (pivot) between Atlas and Axis is known as :
expl: The Atlantoaxial joint is a type of synovial joint that is classified as a biaxial, pivot joint. This joint resides in the upper part of the neck between the first and second cervical vertebrae, also known as the atlas and axis, respectively. It allows for turning of the head from side to side. The pivot joint classification means that it allows for rotation only and is formed by a central pivoting, bony structure that rotates around craniovertebral ligaments.

stem: The joint where the neck joins the head is :
expl: The joint where the neck joins the head is a pivot (pivotal) joint, also known as a rotary joint, allowing for head rotation and some flexion and extension. A pivot joint is a type of synovial joint where a cylindrical bone rotates within a ring-shaped bone, allowing for rotational movement along a single axis.

stem: How many pairs of ribs are there in a human body?
expl: The human rib cage is made up of 12 paired (total 24) rib bones. Each are symmetrically paired in right and left side. The ribs are flat, thin bones that together with the sternum make up the rib cage. The ribs provide protection for vital organs in the upper body, including the heart and lungs.

stem: In human body, leg bone is?
expl: Each human long bone (including leg bone) is composed of a shaft (diaphysis) with two flared ends (epiphysis). The diaphysis resembles a hollow cylinder. It is made of hard compact bone that is resistant to bending. The inner cavity of the diaphysis contains yellow bone marrow that stores fat. The epiphysis is a thin shell of compact bone filled with a lattice or sponge-like structure that is surrounded by red bone marrow (which makes red blood cells).

stem: What is arthroplasty in surgery :
expl: Hip arthroplasty or hip-joint replacement surgery involves replacing components of the hip-joint with a synthetic implant, to repair the damaged part that is causing pain.

stem: The parts of the skeleton that are not as hard as bones and which can be bent are called as :

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Cartilage is a strong, flexible connective tissue that protects our joints and bones. Cartilage is an important structural component of the body. It is a firm tissue but is softer and much more flexible than bone and can be bent. Outer ear and tip of the nose are examples of cartilage. On the other hand, the carpal bones are the eight small bones that make up the wrist (or carpus) that connects the hand to the forearm. These bones are hard and will break if bent. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: The bones are held together by elastic tissues are called–
expl: A ligament is a tissue that connects two bones to form a joint. It is fibrous and dense connective tissue.

stem: Plaques formed on teeth are made up of –

options.label: c
options.text: Food particles plus saliva plus mouth acids

options.label: d
options.text: Food particles plus saliva plus mouth acids plus bateria

expl: Dental plaque is a biofilm or mass of bacteria that grows on surfaces within the mouth. It appears as a white/pale yellow 'slime layer' commonly found in between the teeth and along the cervical margins . Plaques formed on teeth are made up of food particles, saliva, mouth acids and bacteria in the oral cavity. Saliva has a normal pH range of 6.2-7.6 with 6.7 being the average pH.

stem: No pain is felt while cutting the nails because -

options.label: a
options.text: Nails are made of the material of dead cells in which there is no blood circulation.

options.label: b
options.text: Nails are a useless part of the body.

options.label: c
options.text: Nails are made of calcium phosphate.

expl: Nails are usually made up of thick and multiple layers of a type of protein known as α-keratin and are composed of dead tissues. They are devoid of any nerves and blood vessels and therefore we do not feel any pain while the nails are being cut.

stem: Alpha-keratin is a protein, present in :
expl: Alpha-keratin is a family of fibrous structural proteins. It is the key structural material making up the outer (epidermis) layer of human skin. It is the primary component of hair, nails, hooves, and it provides the necessary strength and toughness for masticatory organs, such as the tongue and the hard palate.

stem: Hair is composed of protein called –
expl: Hair is composed of the protein keratin, which is also the primary component of finger and toe nails.

stem: Which one of the following proteins is present in human hair and nails?
expl: Keratin is an extremely strong protein that is a major component in skin, hair, nails, hooves, horns and teeth.

stem: Which of the following are required for the formation of bones and teeth ?
expl: Teeth and bones both are hard, white and heavy. Teeth are composed of calcium, phosphorous and other minerals. Bones contain calcium, phosphorus, sodium and other minerals, but mostly consist of the protein collagen.

stem: Which one of the following nutritional elements is not essential for the formation and strengthening of bones and teeth?
expl: Calcium, phosphorus, and fluorine are essential elements for the formation and strengthening of bones and teeth. Deficiency of these nutritional elements may cause teeth and bone diseases, while iodine is used to control thyroid gland.

stem: The number of teeth that are developed twice in the lifetime of human being is
expl: In human life span, 20 teeth developed twice. Like a human, most of the mammals are diphyodont– It means our 12 permanent molars are monophyodont and others diphyodont. There are four types of teeth– Incisors, canines, premolars and molars.

stem: Which of the following is the strongest part of our body ?
expl: Tooth enamel is the thin outer covering of the tooth and the strongest part of our body. It makes our teeth white and it exists to protect the crowns of healthy teeth. Tooth decay is due to the destruction of tooth enamel. It is made up of hydroxyapatite crystals, which is mainly calcium phosphate.

stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about muscles in human body?

options.label: a
options.text: Muscles can only push the bone.

options.label: c
options.text: Muscles become shorter, stiffer and thicker when contracted.

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Muscles allow a person to move, speak, and chew. They control heartbeat, breathing, and digestion. Other seemingly unrelated functions, including temperature regulation and vision, also rely on the muscular system. Muscles have a range of functions from pumping blood and supporting movement to lifting heavy weights or giving birth. Muscles work by either contracting or relaxing to cause movement. Muscles work in pairs and become shorter, stiffer and thicker when contracted. So, statement of option (a) is incorrect.

stem: Which of the following is the smallest muscle in the human body?
expl: The stapedius muscle in the middle ear is the smallest muscle in the human body. The stapedius is located in the tympanic cavity of the middle ear. It connects the pyramidal eminence of the temporal bone to the neck of the stapes bone. Stapedius muscle stabilizes and controls the vibration of the stapes bone and it is one of the intratympanic muscles for the regulation of sound.

stem: The strongest muscle in human body is found in :
expl: The strongest muscle based on its weight is the masseter, known as jaw muscle. With all muscles of the jaw working together, it can close the teeth with a force as great as about 55 pounds (25 kilograms) on the incisors or about 200 pounds (90.7 kilograms) on the molars.
